title: Rav Chananyah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Bava Metzia 6b: a certain bathhouse over which two were disputing … one of them rose and consecrated it; Rav Chananyah, Rav Oshaya and all the Rabbis withdrew from it. Rav Oshaya said to Rabbah: “When you go before Rav Chisda to Kafri, ask him…”; and Rav Chananyah said to Rabbah: “A baraita was taught that supports you.” Abaye said to him, etc. Likewise in Shevuot 37b he said to Rabbah: “A baraita was taught that supports you”; and in Bava Metzia 31a he said to Rava, “A baraita was taught that supports you,” and in Rabbeinu Chananel’s commentary, the Rosh and Dikdukei Soferim they read that he said it to Rabbah. In Menachot 93a: “Rav Chananyah taught before Rava: An heir does not lay hands,” and Dikdukei Soferim’s reading is “before Rabbah.” In Keritot 7a: “Rav Chananyah taught before Rava: From where do we know that the High Priest,” etc.; Hyman proposes “before Rabbah.” In Eruvin 51a: “Rav Papa said: Rav Chananyah taught.”
Hyman concludes from all this that he was the reciter of baraitot in Rabbah’s academy.

notes.text: Tanna here is the professional reciter of baraitot in an Amora’s academy, not a newly assigned Mishnaic-era date. Hyman’s Rava/Rabbah substitutions remain attributed.

Bava Metzia 6b directly names Chananyah, Oshaya and Rabbah in the bathhouse dispute and the supporting baraita. Hyman’s conclusion that he was the academy’s reciter is retained with its inferential force; exact Rabbeinu Chananel, Rosh and Dikdukei Soferim readings were not independently inspected.
